title: 10 Best Microsoft Teams Apps for Customer Service in 2026
summary: Improve customer service with the 10 best Microsoft Teams apps in 2026. Streamline support, manage tickets, and enhance team collaboration.
body_markdown:
Microsoft Teams has evolved from a collaboration platform into a place where service teams can receive requests, coordinate responses, and manage workflows. For teams already working in Teams, the right customer service app can reduce context-switching while bringing structure to conversations through ticketing, routing, automation, and reporting.


Organizations managing customer service alongside IT, HR, and other service functions can benefit from a platform that brings requests into structured workflows.


The right setup keeps the conversational experience for end users while adding ownership, SLA tracking, escalation paths, and analytics behind the scenes.


## **Key Takeaways**


- Customer service teams should prioritize Teams apps that combine conversational intake with ticketing, AI automation, routing, multi-channel support, and reporting.
- Unthread is the recommended option for organizations that want a unified service experience across Microsoft Teams, Slack, email, and other support channels.
- Unthread's[purpose-built AI agent](https://unthread.io/?ref=unthread.io) can automate repetitive requests, while its broader service management capabilities support workflows across customer service, IT, HR, finance, and operations.
- Teams-native options such as Desk365 and TeamsWork Ticketing are worth considering when keeping service workflows closely connected to Microsoft Teams is a priority.
- The right platform should make submitting a request straightforward while giving service teams the structure needed to assign, track, escalate, and resolve it.


## **What Customer Service Teams Should Look for in a Teams App**


Customer service in Teams requires more than forwarding notifications. Teams need a system that can turn conversations into trackable work, route requests to the appropriate person or team, and provide visibility into service performance.


A strong Microsoft Teams customer service app should help teams:


- Convert conversations into trackable tickets
- Route requests based on topic, priority, context, or ownership
- Automate repetitive requests using AI and knowledge content
- Turn recurring questions into reusable documentation through a[knowledge base](https://unthread.io/products/knowledge-base?ref=unthread.io)
- Track SLAs, response times, and resolution trends
- Connect service workflows with relevant business systems through[integrations](https://unthread.io/products/integrations?ref=unthread.io)


The most practical systems keep intake conversational for users while giving service teams automation, ownership, and reporting behind the scenes.


## **1) Unthread: Best for AI-Native Multi-Channel Service Management**


Unthread is an[AI-native internal service management platform](https://unthread.io/?ref=unthread.io) that helps organizations manage employee requests across Microsoft Teams, Slack, email, and customer portals. It combines conversational ticketing with a[purpose-built AI agent](https://unthread.io/products/agentic-ai?ref=unthread.io) , workflow automation, knowledge management, and analytics.


Unthread turns employee conversations into trackable tickets while maintaining a familiar, conversational experience. Requests can be assigned, prioritized, routed, escalated, and resolved without requiring employees to use a separate help desk portal.


### **Why It Fits Customer Service Teams**


Unthread is particularly useful for organizations managing internal service requests across IT, HR, finance, procurement, legal, and operations. Its automation capabilities support repetitive Tier 1 requests, including access management, onboarding, policy questions, and internal approvals.


The platform also supports customer-facing service workflows, allowing teams to coordinate external requests alongside internal operations.


Its[workflow automations](https://unthread.io/products/automations?ref=unthread.io) help teams manage recurring requests, approvals, routing, escalations, and follow-ups while reducing manual administration.


### **Customer Service Capabilities**


- Purpose-built AI agent for triage, routing, and automated resolution
- Multi-channel intake across Microsoft Teams, Slack, email, and customer portals
- Automated ticket assignment and escalation
- Self-learning documentation based on recurring support conversations
- [AI analytics](https://unthread.io/products/analytics?ref=unthread.io) for identifying service trends and automation opportunities
- SLA and SLO tracking
- Customer portal and live chat capabilities
- Bring-your-own-LLM support through MCP
- Integrations with Jira, Salesforce, Zendesk, ServiceNow, and HubSpot


Unthread's AI helped Lemonade automatically resolve approximately[40% of tickets](https://unthread.io/blog/case-study-how-lemonade-boosts-efficiency-with-unthread-and-gen-ai/) across internal service teams.


### **What Teams Should Consider**


Unthread is a strong fit for organizations looking to automate internal support while connecting service workflows across multiple communication channels.


Its[Pro plan](https://unthread.io/pricing?ref=unthread.io) starts at $70 per agent/month, with Enterprise plans offering additional capabilities such as SSO, custom integrations, and advanced support.


## **2) Zendesk**


Zendesk is a customer service platform used for managing support requests across multiple communication channels. Organizations already using Zendesk may consider its Microsoft Teams capabilities when they want Teams conversations and ticket activity to connect with their existing customer support environment.


### **Key Features**


- Omnichannel customer support workflows
- Ticket routing and workflow rules
- Knowledge management
- AI-assisted support capabilities
- Reporting and analytics
- Broad integration ecosystem


### **Considerations**


Zendesk is primarily a standalone customer service platform, so teams should assess how much of their daily workflow they want to manage directly from Microsoft Teams versus the Zendesk interface.


## **3) Freshdesk**


Freshdesk is a cloud-based customer service platform from Freshworks that connects ticket management with communication and collaboration tools such as Microsoft Teams.


It can suit organizations that already use Freshdesk and want agents to receive ticket activity and coordinate service work through Teams.


### **Key Features**


- Ticket creation and management
- Workflow automation
- AI-assisted customer service
- Knowledge management
- Ticket notifications in Teams
- Reporting and analytics


### **Considerations**


Teams should evaluate how deeply their required workflows operate inside Microsoft Teams and which activities are still handled within Freshdesk.


## **4) InvGate Service Management**


InvGate Service Management is an IT service management platform that supports conversational request handling through Microsoft Teams.


Its Virtual Service Agent can provide users with a conversational path for requesting help, finding knowledge, and creating service requests. Although its core positioning is centered on ITSM, the structured workflows can also be relevant when customer service teams coordinate with technical or internal service functions.


### **Key Features**


- Conversational service requests
- AI-assisted self-service
- Knowledge-based responses
- Structured ticket workflows
- ITIL-aligned service management
- Request routing and management


### **Considerations**


Organizations should evaluate whether an ITSM-oriented workflow matches the processes their customer service teams need to manage.


## **5) Social Intents**


Social Intents focuses on bringing website live chat conversations directly into collaboration platforms such as Microsoft Teams.


It can fit organizations that want customer-facing website chat to reach employees inside the environment where they already communicate rather than requiring agents to work from another chat interface.


### **Key Features**


- Website live chat connected to Teams
- Customizable chat widgets
- Real-time customer conversations
- AI-assisted chat capabilities
- Conversation routing into Teams


### **Considerations**


Social Intents is primarily centered on live chat. Teams that need broader ticketing, SLA management, cross-functional workflows, or service management capabilities should evaluate how it fits alongside their existing systems.


## **6) Desk365**


Desk365 is a Microsoft Teams-focused help desk platform designed to bring conversational ticketing into the Microsoft ecosystem.


It is particularly relevant for organizations using Teams for employee service and internal help desk workflows, although teams can assess its functionality against their broader customer service requirements.


### **Key Features**


- Microsoft Teams-based ticketing
- Conversational request management
- Ticket assignment and tracking
- AI-assisted ticket deflection
- Workflow automation
- Internal service desk functionality


### **Considerations**


Desk365 has a strong internal support orientation. Organizations primarily managing external customer interactions should evaluate whether its workflows align with the customer-facing channels and service processes they require.


## **7) HappyFox**


HappyFox is a help desk platform for managing requests across channels such as email, chat, web portals, and other service touchpoints.


For Microsoft Teams users, it can provide a way to connect ticket activity with the collaboration environment while retaining HappyFox as the primary help desk system.


### **Key Features**


- Omnichannel ticket management
- Workflow automation
- Knowledge management
- Ticket notifications and actions
- Customer service reporting
- Automated routing rule


### **Considerations**


Teams should determine how much of their required ticket lifecycle can be managed from Microsoft Teams and how frequently agents will need to move into the main HappyFox interface.


## **8) Tikit**


Tikit is a service desk platform designed around Microsoft Teams and the broader Microsoft 365 ecosystem.


Its Microsoft-oriented architecture can make it relevant for organizations already standardized on Microsoft technologies and looking to connect service management with their existing identity, endpoint management, and collaboration environment.


### **Key Features**


- Teams-based service workflows
- AI-assisted virtual agent capabilities
- Microsoft Entra ID connectivity
- Microsoft Intune connectivity
- Microsoft 365-oriented service management
- Self-service workflows


### **Considerations**


Organizations should compare the depth of Tikit's service management functionality with the complexity of their customer service processes, integrations, and reporting requirements.


## **9) TeamsWork Ticketing**


TeamsWork Ticketing is designed to let organizations create and manage tickets from within Microsoft Teams.


It can be relevant for teams that want their ticketing workflows to remain closely connected to Teams rather than introducing a separate primary interface for employees or agents.


### **Key Features**


- Ticket creation inside Teams
- Assignment and status tracking
- Multiple ticketing instances
- Department-specific workflows
- Teams-based request management


### **Considerations**


Teams should evaluate how the platform handles their requirements for automation, analytics, integrations, knowledge management, and multi-channel intake as service operations expand.


## **10) Fireflies.ai**


Fireflies.ai is an AI meeting assistant rather than a traditional help desk. Its relevance to customer service comes from documenting conversations that happen through Microsoft Teams meetings.


Teams can use meeting transcripts, summaries, searchable conversation histories, and action items to retain context from customer calls and support follow-ups.


### **Key Features**


- Automatic meeting transcription
- AI-generated summaries
- Action-item extraction
- Searchable meeting history
- Keyword and conversation search


### **Considerations**


Fireflies.ai addresses meeting documentation rather than service desk management. Organizations needing structured ticketing, SLA tracking, routing, and request automation will generally need a dedicated service management platform alongside it.

## **Frequently Asked Questions**


### **How do Microsoft Teams apps improve customer service efficiency?**


Microsoft Teams apps can reduce context-switching by bringing conversations, notifications, ticket actions, and service workflows closer to where teams already collaborate. More advanced platforms can also convert conversations into structured tickets, automate routing, track ownership, and connect requests with other business systems.


### **What features should customer service teams look for in a Microsoft Teams app?**


Customer service teams should consider integration depth, ticket management, routing, AI automation, knowledge management, SLA tracking, analytics, and multi-channel support. The best fit depends on whether Teams will be the primary service interface or one channel within a larger help desk environment.


### **Can AI automate customer service workflows in Microsoft Teams?**


Yes. AI agents can use knowledge content and request context to answer repetitive questions, categorize requests, route tickets, trigger workflows, and determine when human intervention is required. Unthread's purpose-built AI agent has helped Lemonade automatically resolve approximately[40% of tickets](https://unthread.io/blog/case-study-how-lemonade-boosts-efficiency-with-unthread-and-gen-ai/) across multiple service teams.


### **How does native Teams-ticketing differ from notification integrations?**


A deeper Teams integration can let users create, update, assign, and manage requests from conversations, while basic integrations may primarily send ticket notifications into Teams. Organizations should evaluate exactly which parts of the ticket lifecycle can be completed without switching interfaces.


### **What security factors should organizations review?**


Organizations should evaluate data handling, identity and access controls, SSO, user provisioning, AI data practices, compliance requirements, and vendor security processes. Unthread maintains[SOC 2 Type II](https://unthread.io/security?ref=unthread.io) compliance and offers HIPAA compliance with BAAs for Enterprise customers.
